evidence.excerpt: The Landau–Vishkin algorithm is a family of exact, parameter-sensitive methods for edit distance and approximate string matching developed by Gad M. Landau and Uzi Vishkin during the 1980s. Its central idea is to stop evaluating the dynamic-programming matrix cell by cell. Instead, the algorithm tracks only the farthest-reaching edit path on each relevant diagonal and uses longest common extension queries to jump across arbitrarily long runs of exact matches in a single operation.

Instead of computing an edit-distance matrix independently for every candidate string, the allowed edit neighborhood of the pattern is compiled into an automaton. A candidate is accepted precisely when its sequence of symbols drives the automaton into an accepting state.
